@graph.headline: Layers of the Eye: All Three Coats in Exam-Level Detail
@graph.description: Master the three layers of the eye—fibrous, vascular and neural—with anatomy, histology, embryology, clinical correlations, viva traps and MCQs.

mainEntity.name: What are the three layers of the eye?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are the outer fibrous coat, middle vascular coat or uvea, and inner neural coat or retina.

mainEntity.name: Which layer of the eye contains the retina?

acceptedAnswer.text: The retina forms the inner neural coat.

mainEntity.name: Is the choroid part of the retina?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The choroid is the posterior portion of the middle vascular coat and supplies the outer retina.

mainEntity.name: Where does the cornea become sclera?

acceptedAnswer.text: They meet at the corneoscleral limbus.

mainEntity.name: What separates the retina from the choroid?

acceptedAnswer.text: The RPE is apposed to Bruch membrane at the interface with the choriocapillaris.
